articles.author: Jonathan Wilson
articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
articles.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

articles.title: Emery insists no change of plan for Aston Villa despite fears over Galatasaray surface
articles.description: ‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions League game at ­Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”. Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work. Galatasaray played Saturday’s victory over Samsunspor at Basaksehir Fatih Terim stadium, a significantly smaller ground named after the former Turkey manager, who played for and managed Galatasaray. Continue reading...

articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino said after game it was ‘never a foul’ ‘No one’s coming to save us,’ admits Kobbie Mainoo Manchester United intend to appeal against the red card Leny Yoro received in the eighth minute of the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. The defender was dismissed after fouling Alexander Isak outside the penalty area but Mauricio Pochettino believes the striker would not have reached the ball to take him through on goal against Senne Lammens and therefore it was not worthy of a sending-off . Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul.” Continue reading...

articles.title: Esposito emulates Vieri with Inter hat-trick but De Ketelaere haunts him again
articles.description: Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born. We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France . articles.author: Andy Brassell
articles.title: Jamal Musiala controversy the nadir of Bayern Munich’s turbulent week
articles.description: German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat. The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too. Continue reading...

articles.title: WSL talking points: Captain Spence inspires Spurs shock win at City and Lionesses impress
articles.description: We may have a proper title race on our hands as City and Chelsea drop points and LCL strengthen their grip on third place Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a shock 3-1 victory away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. articles.author: Guardian sport
articles.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
articles.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...
